questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement."

Cancer is not a contagious disease, is it?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'No improvement'.

Key Points

  • Here in the given sentence, the correct question tag has been used.
  • If the sentence is positive, the question tag must be negative and vice versa.
  • Always use pronoun in the question tag.
  • For the negative question tag, use the contracted form of 'helping verb' and 'not'.
    • Example: didn't, won't, etc.
  • Here the given sentence is negative, so here positive question tag will be used.
  • This sentence does not require any correction.

The correct sentence is: Cancer is not a contagious disease, is it?

Additional Information

  •  What is a question tag?
    • ​A question tag is a confirmatory question asked from the second person.​

questions.text:
Which of the phrases given below the sentence should replace the word/phrase underlined in the sentence to make it grammatically correct? If the sentence is correct as it is given and no correction is required, mark 'No correction required' as the answer.

I am weak in Maths and I can't perform well on hand.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: at; off hand.
Key Points
  • 'at' will replace 'in'; 'off hand' will replace 'on hand'.
  • The preposition 'at' agrees with good and bad in sentences like:
    • I am good at English.
    • I am bad at Maths.
  • The idiom 'off hand' means without preparation or delay.
  • Remember, 'off hand' is an adverb.
    • For example: I prepared the extempore off hand.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is: I am weak at Maths and I can't perform well off hand.
​Additional Information
  • At is also used to address a specific location.
    • For example: I am at the airport.
  • At is also used in idioms like:
    • at bay: At a distance.
    • at arm's length: At a distance
    • at any rate: whatever happens or is happening
    • at one's disposal: available for one's use
    • at fault: causing a problem or accident
    • at first: in the beginning
    • at last: finally, after some delay
    • at a loss: unsure of what to do or say; speechless

questions.text:
A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part, which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to 'No improvement'.

There was a windfall on several uncapped players too.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is windfall for. 

Key Points

  • The error lies in the usage of the preposition on instead of for.
  • The preposition for is used to show who or what is to receive something.
    • Example: There's a letter for you.
  • ​Here, we have to use the preposition for to show that a windfall is to be received by several uncapped players.

Hence, the correct sentence is: There was a windfall for several uncapped players too. 

Important Points

  • Let's look at the other cases where preposition on is used:
  • about concerning a person/topic/subject
    This is a good book on Maths.
    to suggest a direction
    Rahul was hit on the head.
    to indicate engagements
    He is there on some business.
    to show the stillness of something while touching/covering a surface
    Veebha was lying on the bed because of viral fever.
    to indicate a day/date
    He is returning on the 7th instant.

 

  • Let's look at the other cases where preposition for is used:
  • to indicate a destination
    Satan left for Los Angeles today.
    to indicate a motive/purpose
     I go for a walk daily.
    to indicate liking/suitability
    The climate of Delhi is bad for health.
    in the sense of preparation
    We should save for the future.

Additional Information

  • Let's understand the meaning of the word:
    • Windfall: an unexpected, unearned, or sudden gain or advantage.
    • Example: They received a windfall because of the tax cuts.
    • Synonyms: felicity, godsend, manna
    • Antonyms: affliction, bane, scourge

questions.text:
Which of the following phrases (1), (2), (3), (4) given below in the statement should replace the phrase printed in bold in the sentence to make it grammatically correct? If the sentence is correct as it is given and ‘No Correction is required’, mark (5) as the answer.

The alternative is letting the most vulnerable among us fall into an economic abyss, through no fault of their own.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is No Correction Required.

Key Points

  • The sentence is contextually and grammatically correct. 
  • Let's see the meaning of the prepositions used:
    • The meaning of the preposition among is 'in the middle or included in a larger group of people or things'. Among is commonly followed by a plural noun phrase.
      • Example: The house is nestled among the trees.
    • The meaning of the preposition On refers a 'surface of something'
      • Example- I kept the dishes on the dining table.
    • The meaning of the preposition above is when 'something directly over it or higher than it.' 
      • Example- He lifted his hands above his head.
    • The meaning of the preposition between means 'among two people or things'
      • Example- The money was divided equally between Raja and Naresh.
    • The meaning of the preposition For is to 'indicate the duration or time' 
      • Example- I attended the session for one year only.

Hence, option 5 is correct.

Additional Information

  • We use between to refer to two things which are clearly separated.
  • We use among to talk about things which are not clearly separated because they are part of a group or crowd or mass of objects.
    • Example- Our holiday house is between the mountains and the sea. (the mountains are on one side and the sea is on the other)
    • Example- The ancient fountain was hidden among the trees. (surrounded by trees)

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

No sooner did the officer enter the office then the employees stood up.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'than'.
  • Here in the sentence, 'then' is used which is wrong.
  • No sooner is used to show that one thing happens immediately after another thing.
  • It is usually followed by 'than'.
    • ​Example- No sooner had I closed my eyes than I fell asleep.
  • Here in the sentence 'no sooner' is followed by 'then'.
  • It should be replaced by 'than'.
The correct sentence : No sooner did the officer enter the office than the employees stood up.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement."

Somebody entered the gate, do it?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'didn't they?'.

Key Points

  • Here in the given sentence, the wrong question tag has been used.
  • If the sentence is positive, the question tag must be negative and vice versa.
  • Always use pronoun in the question tag.
  • For the negative question tag, use the contracted form of 'helping verb' and 'not'.
    • Example: didn't, won't, etc.
  • Here the given sentence is positive, so here negative question tag will be used.
  • Each, every, everyone, no one, nobody, none, someone, somebody, everyone, everybody, etc are singular and hence will take singular verb, singular pronoun and singular adjective with them but their question tag will take plural verb and plural pronoun.
  • Here in the given sentence somebody will take a plural pronoun in the question tag. So, 'it' will replaced by 'they'.
  • Sentence is in past tense so question tag will also be in past tense. So, 'do' will be replaced by 'didn't.

The correct answer: Somebody entered the gate, didn't they?

Additional Information 

  •  What is a question tag?
    • ​A question tag is a confirmatory question asked from the second person.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

If he will work hard he will surely get the job of his choice.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'works'.
  • Here in the sentence, 'will work' has been used which is wrong.
  • If two actions take place one after the other in the future, and if the second action depends on the first action, the first action is in simple present tense and the second action is in the simple future tense.
  • Example- She will come to meet you as soon as you reach Delhi.
  • Here in the given sentence, if he will work hard first then only he will get a job. So, the first action should be in the simple present tense.
  • So, 'will work'  will be replaced by 'works'
The correct sentence: If he works hard he will surely get the job of his choice.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

I am done in him because he is not loyal.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'done with'.
  • Here in the given sentence, 'done in' used which is wrong.
  • Done with means have no relation.
    • Example-  I am done with my husband.
  • Done in and done for means to be ruined.
    • Example-  He appears to be done for since he has lost heavily in gambling.
  • In the given sentence it is about that person is not loyal so I have no relations with him.
  • So, 'done in' will be replaced by 'done with'.
The correct sentence: I am done with him because he is not loyal.

questions.text:
Which of the phrases 1, 2, 3 and 4 given below should replace the phrase given in bold in the following sentence to make the sentence grammatically correct? If the sentence is correct as it is and ' No correction is required ' choose option 5 as an option.

Mahatma Gandhi say that honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is says that.

  • The Plural verb say does not appear to agree with the singular subject Mahatma Gandhi. 
  • According to the Subject-Verb agreement rule, a verb must be in accordance with the noun. A singular noun must be followed by a singular verb and a plural noun by a plural verb.
  • The correct sentence will be "Mahatma Gandhi says that honesty is the best policy."  

​Important Points

  • For option (1)  - The Plural verb speak does not appear to agree with the singular subject, Mahatma Gandhi. Hence, options (1) and (4) are incorrect.
  • For option (2) ie. were saying - This is incorrect as we cannot use the plural form of 'was' when we are talking about a singular subject.
  • Therefore, option (3) - says that is the most suitable option.


In present tenses, nouns and verbs form plurals in opposite ways:  

nouns ADD an s to the singular form, BUT verbs REMOVE an s from the singular form.

Mistake Points

This is a tricky question.

Here, we will not consider whether Mahatma Gandhi was a person who had said something decades ago.  According to the context, 'says' and 'said' both are correct. Since we don't have 'said' in the option, we'll go with 'says'- which is correct according to the subject-verb agreement in this case.

A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

Though he worked hard yet he failed.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'No Improvement'.
  • Here in the given sentence, 'Though' is used which is right.
  • Hence, it does not require any correction.
  • When conjunctions are in pairs, the pair must be correct.
  • When 'though' is used in a sentence then it should be paired with 'yet'.
  • Here in the given sentence, 'though' is correctly paired with 'yet'.
The correct sentence: Though he worked yet he failed.
